function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑use set of files** that you can drop into the `nodejs-welcome` repository, add to Git, commit, and push.  
I’ve kept the Docker image lightweight, exposed the typical Node.js port (3000), and created a minimal Kubernetes deployment + service.  
The GitHub Actions workflow builds the image and pushes it to **GitHub Container Registry** (you can swap it for Docker Hub if you prefer).

> **NOTE** – I can’t actually clone or push to your repo from here, but the commands below will get you there once you run them locally.

---

## 1️⃣ Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Maintainer
LABEL maintainer="Unknown"

# Working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["npm", "start"]
```

> *Why this Dockerfile?*  
> * `node:18-alpine` is small and includes the latest LTS Node.js.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a clean install from `package-lock.json`.  
> * The app is started with `npm start`, which is the conventional entrypoint for Node projects.

---

## 2️⃣ Kubernetes YAML

Create a file named `k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml` (or split into `deployment.yaml` & `service.yaml` if you prefer):

```yaml
# k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/<YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace <YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME>
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> *What to change:*  
> * Replace `<YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME>` with your GitHub username (or any registry you’re using).  
> * If you want a `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer`, change `type` accordingly.

---

## 3️⃣ GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the file `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build the Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} \
            .

      # Push the image
      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
```

> *Why this workflow?*  
> * It triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` to authenticate to GHCR (no extra secrets needed).  
> * Tags the image with both `latest` and the commit SHA for traceability.

---

## 4️⃣ Add, Commit & Push

Open a terminal in the root of the cloned repository and run:

```bash
# 1️⃣ Add the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml

# 2️⃣ Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# 3️⃣ Push to main
git push origin main
```

If you’re using a different branch name or remote, adjust the commands accordingly.

---

## 5️⃣ Verify

1. **Docker image** – After the push, check GHCR (or your chosen registry) for the `nodejs-welcome` image.  
2. **Kubernetes** – Apply the manifest:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml
   ```

   Then verify pods and service:

   ```bash
   kubectl get pods
   kubectl get svc
   ```

3. **GitHub Actions** – Go to *Actions* tab → *Build & Push Docker Image* → confirm the job succeeded.

---

### Quick Recap

| Step | Command / File |
|------|----------------|
| 1 | `git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git` |
| 2 | Add `Dockerfile`, `k8s-nodejs-welcome.yaml`, `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml` |
| 3 | `git add ...` |
| 4 | `git commit -m "..."` |
| 5 | `git push origin main` |

That’s it! Your repo now contains a production‑ready Dockerfile, Kubernetes deployment/service, and a CI pipeline that automatically builds and publishes the image whenever you push to `main`. Happy coding!
